title: Level-0 Lattice Under Specialization to a Face
body_html:
Level-0 Lattice Under Specialization to a Face

Let \(G=\operatorname{Sp}(W)\), let \(x\) lie in an open facet \(F\) of \(\mathcal B(\operatorname{Sp}(W))\), and let \(y\in\overline F\) (so \(\operatorname{facet}(y)\le F\)). Then \[ \mathscr L_{x,0}\subseteq\mathscr L_{y,0}, \] with equality in a hyperbolic-plane slot \(H_i\) unless the corresponding coordinate of \(y\) is an integer (a level-\(0\) jump of \(\mathscr L_y\) in \(H_i\)).
proof_html:
By Bruhat-Tits the facet closure \(\overline F\) lies in an apartment; fix one, \(\mathcal A\), attached to a maximal split torus, with associated Witt basis \(\{e_i,f_i\}_{i=1}^n\) (Broussous-Stevens, Sections 2-4). In this chart the points of \(\mathcal A\) are tuples \(\underline a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\) and the self-dual lattice function of \(\underline a\) is \[ \mathscr L_{\underline a,s}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\big(\mathfrak p^{\lceil s-a_i\rceil}e_i\oplus\mathfrak p^{\lceil s+a_i\rceil}f_i\big) \] (Apartment Model for Sp(W) via Self-Dual Lattice Functions: the Broussous-Stevens norm \(\alpha_p\) read as a lattice function, in the sign convention fixed there; self-dual by Self-Dual Lattice Function). Both \(x,y\in\overline F\subseteq\mathcal A\), so both lattice functions are split by this basis. Write \(a_i=a_i(x)\) and \(b_i=a_i(y)\). Reading the formula at \(s=0\), \[ \mathscr L_{x,0}=\bigoplus_i\big(\mathfrak p^{\lceil -a_i\rceil}e_i\oplus\mathfrak p^{\lceil a_i\rceil}f_i\big), \qquad \mathscr L_{y,0}=\bigoplus_i\big(\mathfrak p^{\lceil -b_i\rceil}e_i\oplus\mathfrak p^{\lceil b_i\rceil}f_i\big), \] and, since a larger \(\mathfrak p\)-power is a smaller lattice, \(\mathscr L_{x,0}\subseteq\mathscr L_{y,0}\) is equivalent to \[ \lceil -a_i\rceil\ge\lceil -b_i\rceil\quad\text{and}\quad\lceil a_i\rceil\ge\lceil b_i\rceil\qquad(\forall i).\tag{$\ast$} \]

The jumps of \(\mathscr L_{\underline a}\) in \(s\) lie at \(s\equiv a_i\) and \(s\equiv -a_i\pmod 1\) (the \(e_i\)- and \(f_i\)-lines). Two of them collide — so the lattice chain, hence the facet of \(\underline a\), changes — across \(a_i\equiv -a_i\), i.e. across each hyperplane \(\{a_i=\tfrac m2\}\) (\(m\in\mathbb Z\)); each is therefore a wall (the affine \(C_n\)-wall of the long root \(2\epsilon_i\); Broussous-Stevens, Section 4). A facet meets no wall transversally: it lies in a closed alcove face and is disjoint from every wall not containing it (Bruhat-Tits). Fix \(i\); there are two cases.

  • (degenerate) Some wall \(\{a_i=\tfrac m2\}\) contains \(F\): then \(a_i\equiv\tfrac m2\) on \(\overline F\), so \(b_i=a_i\) and \((\ast)\) holds with equality in slot \(i\).
  • (non-degenerate) No such wall contains \(F\): then \(F\) is disjoint from every \(\{a_i=\tfrac m2\}\); since \(a_i\) is affine and \(F\) convex and connected, \(a_i(F)\) is an interval meeting no \(\tfrac m2\), so \(a_i\in(\tfrac k2,\tfrac{k+1}2)\) for a single \(k=k_i\in\mathbb Z\). As \(a_i\) is affine and \(\overline F\) compact convex, \(a_i(\overline F)=\overline{a_i(F)}\), hence \(b_i\in[\tfrac k2,\tfrac{k+1}2]\).

In the non-degenerate case the open interval \((\tfrac{k}{2},\tfrac{k+1}{2})\) has length \(\tfrac12\) and contains no integer, so \(\lceil a_i\rceil\) and \(\lceil -a_i\rceil\) are constant on it. Split on the parity of \(k\):

  • \(k=2\ell\): then \(a_i\in(\ell,\ell+\tfrac12)\), so \(\lceil a_i\rceil=\ell+1\) and \(\lceil -a_i\rceil=-\ell\). As \(b_i\in[\ell,\ell+\tfrac12]\) we get \(\lceil b_i\rceil\in\{\ell,\ell+1\}\le\ell+1\) and \(\lceil -b_i\rceil=-\ell\).
  • \(k=2\ell+1\): then \(a_i\in(\ell+\tfrac12,\ell+1)\), so \(\lceil a_i\rceil=\ell+1\) and \(\lceil -a_i\rceil=-\ell\). As \(b_i\in[\ell+\tfrac12,\ell+1]\) we get \(\lceil b_i\rceil=\ell+1\) and \(\lceil -b_i\rceil\in\{-\ell-1,-\ell\}\le-\ell\).

In both cases \((\ast)\) holds, so \(\mathscr L_{x,0}\subseteq\mathscr L_{y,0}\). In a non-degenerate slot a strict inequality occurs iff \(b_i\) is the integer endpoint of \([\tfrac{k}{2},\tfrac{k+1}{2}]\) (namely \(b_i=\ell\) for \(k=2\ell\), or \(b_i=\ell+1\) for \(k=2\ell+1\)), i.e. iff \(b_i\in\mathbb Z\) — equivalently \(0\) is a jump of \(\mathscr L_y\) in \(H_i\). \(\square\)

Corollary

Applying the duality \(\#\) (which reverses inclusions and sends \(\mathscr L_{\bullet,0}\) to \(\mathscr L_{\bullet,0+}\)) gives \(\mathscr L_{y,0+}\subseteq\mathscr L_{x,0+}\), hence the four-term chain \[ \mathscr L_{y,0+}\ \subseteq\ \mathscr L_{x,0+}\ \subseteq\ \mathscr L_{x,0}\ \subseteq\ \mathscr L_{y,0}. \] Thus \(\mathsf b_x=\mathscr L_{x,0}/\mathscr L_{x,0+}\) is a symplectic subquotient \(U^{\perp}/U\) of \(\mathsf b_y=\mathscr L_{y,0}/\mathscr L_{y,0+}\), with \(U=\mathscr L_{x,0+}/\mathscr L_{y,0+}\) isotropic — the level-\(0\) input to the parabolic and flag attached to the incidence.
